Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Outline of National History, Introduction and files it under Modern Chinese Thought. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Qian Mu

Qian Mu (1895–1990) was a leading modern historian of Chinese thought who defended the continuity of China’s cultural tradition amid revolution and Westernization. Largely self-taught, he taught in mainland universities before settling in Hong Kong and later Taiwan.

How to read this passage

Is time a river, a dimension, or a structure of consciousness? Augustine, Bergson, and modern metaphysics offer rival pictures while ethics asks how finite time should be spent. This passage enters that discussion through time, society, dignity.

Concepts in this quote

Time
Philosophy of time asks what tense and duration are—and how memory, death, and history shape a human life.
Society
Society is the web of institutions, customs, and mutual expectations in which individual freedom takes shape.
Dignity
Dignity names the worth that persons claim simply as persons—and the respect that worth demands.
